observation.visible_scene: A night-sky fireworks display filmed against a black background. A fan-shaped ground fountain of golden sparks sits at the bottom center throughout the early part, a thin horizontal power line crosses the middle of the frame, and a band of small blue-white dot sparks spans the center. Above them, several aerial bursts bloom and fade.
visible_changes: At t=0 two small white starbursts are already open at the top; by t=0.13–0.20 they expand into larger golden radial bursts and a third burst appears at right.
Around t=0.20–0.27 a very bright white flash erupts at the right, briefly lighting up smoke and the power line, then subsides.
From t=0.33 onward multiple golden radial starbursts spread across the upper half; the central blue-dot band fades out.
From t=0.53 to t=1.2 the golden streaks develop dense hanging clusters of white 'chrysanthemum/willow' dots that twinkle and slowly dim; the bottom golden fountain fades to smoke.
From t=1.3 to t=2.3 the aerial clusters decay into sparse, faint twinkling points against black sky (a static, fading interval).
From t=2.4 to t=2.67 a new bright white fountain/flash ignites at the bottom center, growing and producing smoke, while the upper points remain faint.
The bursts grow by radial expansion from their centers rather than by translating across the frame; the bottom fountain stays at a fixed position.
outside_clip_unknowns: The cause or ignition of the new bottom fountain near the end and whether it continues after t=2.67.
What preceded the already-open bursts at t=0 and the final outcome of the fading aerial points.
The source of the bright white flash at t=0.2–0.27 and any related launch.
uncertain_details: Camera motion: the power line and fountain positions stay roughly consistent, so the camera is likely static, but this cannot be confirmed from background evidence alone.
Whether the bottom golden feature is a ground fountain or a reflection is not fully determinable; it is treated as a fixed-position luminous effect.
The slow downward drift of some white dots could be gravity or fade-out; only their gradual dimming is clearly supported.
